abstract:
Small businesses produce almost half of the gross domestic product of Kyrgyzstan, and their customers increasingly
write to them in WhatsApp, Instagram and Telegram. With one administrator and no one at the desk in the evening or on
days off, many messages are answered late or not at all, and the customer goes to a competitor. Large language models
can hold such conversations, but a general-purpose chatbot may invent prices or availability, is weaker in Kyrgyz than
in Russian or English, and does not act on the business's real schedule and stock.

This thesis proposes \textbf{Joop AI}, an extensible platform of AI agents that answers the customers of small
businesses in Kyrgyz and Russian across Telegram, WhatsApp, Instagram and a web chat. Its central design principle is
that \emph{the model proposes and the code decides}: the language model holds the conversation and proposes bookings,
orders and hand-offs, and the platform executes each of them only after validating it against the business's own data,
claiming time slots atomically so that double bookings are impossible. Sector packs adapt the same platform to twenty
kinds of businesses, and a self-service web panel lets a non-technical owner set it up without integration work.

Following design science research, the study builds the platform iteratively and evaluates it with 310 scripted
bilingual conversations checked automatically against the real model, a native-speaker review of Kyrgyz replies, and
pilot deployments that measure customers served outside working hours, bookings made by the agent and the cost of each
conversation.
